h1: Solar System for Mosque or Shop: Size, Panels and Inverter
author: ali-ahmad

fields.name: loads
fields.label: Appliances the solar system must run
fields.hint: The list starts as a small mosque with one hall. For a shop, remove the rows and add your lights, fans, fridge or freezer, computer and AC. Set the hours a day each one runs: fans and lights through each prayer, ACs mainly at Zuhr, Asr and Isha, with Friday's longer Jummah averaged over the week.

fields.label: Performance ratio

fields.label: Inverter safety margin

outputs.label: Energy the building uses a day
Units the system makes a month

answer: A small one-hall mosque with ceiling fans, tube lights, 1.5 ton inverter ACs, a water pump, a dispenser and a sound system needs about {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of solar ({{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w|int}} W) with a {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter in Lahore. System size is the larger of daily units ÷ sun yield and running watts ÷ performance ratio.
how: Energy: each appliance's watts × quantity × hours a day (inverter ACs at their average draw), added up = {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day; ÷ {{out.yield_kwh_per_kwp_day|1}} units per kW of panels a day for your city = {{out.kw_energy|2}} kW. Power: {{out.running_w|int}} W running load ÷ {{out.pr|2}} performance ratio = {{out.kw_power|2}} kW, so the panels can carry everything at Zuhr or at the shop's midday peak. The larger, {{out.kw|2}} kW, needs {{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w}} W = {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW, about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month. Inverter: the larger of {{out.running_w|int}} W × {{out.margin|2}} = {{out.inverter_kw_load|2}} kW for the load and {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels ÷ {{out.dc_ac_ratio_max|1}} = {{out.inverter_kw_array|2}} kW, so the panels are never more than {{out.dc_ac_ratio_max|1}} times the inverter: {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW continuous, with a surge rating of at least {{out.inverter_surge_w|int}} W.
key_facts: A small one-hall mosque in Lahore with fans, lights, 1.5 ton inverter ACs, a water pump, a dispenser and a sound system runs about {{out.running_w|int}} W and uses about {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day, so it needs about {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of solar and a {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter.

A small shop open all day with lights, fans, a deep freezer, a computer, CCTV and Wi-Fi uses about {{ex.2.out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day and needs about {{ex.2.out.installed_kw|2}} kW of solar with a {{ex.2.out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter.
Adding a 1.5 ton inverter AC for most of the opening hours to that shop raises the need to about {{ex.3.out.installed_kw|2}} kW of solar and a {{ex.3.out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter.
The mosque and shop load lists on this page are Wattlyst estimates from typical fit-outs, not measurements of any one building; change every row to match yours before you ask for quotes.

formula.text: kW = max(E_day ÷ yield, P_run ÷ 1000 ÷ PR); panels = ceil(kW × 1000 ÷ W_panel)
lines: E_day = Σ (watts × qty × hours) ÷ 1000, units used a day
yield = units one kW of panels makes a day in your city
P_run = total running watts, PR = performance ratio
Inverter W = max(P_run × margin, kW × 1000 ÷ r_max), r_max = largest panel-to-inverter (DC/AC) ratio; surge ≥ largest starting load
Battery Ah = P_run × night hours ÷ (V × DoD × η)

sections.h2: Solar system for mosque: sized around prayer times
p: A mosque's load comes in blocks: fans and lights through each congregation, ACs mainly for Zuhr, Asr and Isha in summer, the water pump for wudu, and a longer, fuller Jummah once a week. The default list averages those hours over the week. It is a Wattlyst estimate for a small one-hall mosque, not a survey of mosques, so change the counts and hours to match yours.

Zuhr and Asr fall in full sun, so the panels carry those prayers directly. Fajr, Maghrib and Isha are in the dark, so their load comes from the grid or a battery. That is why the power rule, {{out.running_w|int}} W ÷ {{out.pr|2}}, decides the panel size here: {{out.kw_power|2}} kW against {{out.kw_energy|2}} kW from the energy rule.

A shop's load follows its opening hours, and most of them are in daylight, which suits solar well. The small-shop list (lights, fans, a deep freezer, a computer, CCTV and Wi-Fi through the opening hours) needs {{ex.2.out.installed_kw|2}} kW with a {{ex.2.out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter. With an inverter AC the need rises to {{ex.3.out.installed_kw|2}} kW and {{ex.3.out.inverter_kw|2}} kW.

A freezer or a cold drinks fridge runs day and night. If the shop is closed at night and the grid is off, the freezer needs a battery or it warms up; add backup hours above, but list only the freezer, CCTV and router for that battery.

sections.h2: Commercial solar calculator for a small building: what changes
p: The sizing is the same as for a house; only the load list and the hours change. What differs is the bill: shops are on the commercial tariff and some mosques have their own arrangements, while our tariff data covers domestic connections only. This page therefore sizes the system but does not compute the bill saving; take the units a month from the result and your rate from your bill.
A building that is empty at night but busy at midday gets more from solar than a house, because more of its units are used directly instead of exported at the buyback rate.

sections.h2: What does a solar system for a mosque or shop cost?
p: We do not print a price on this page because panel and inverter prices move with the dollar rate. The solar price estimator gives the current range for a {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW system from dated price lists, and the quote checker compares a quote you have against that range.

A complete quote includes the panels, the inverter, mounting structure, DC and AC cables, breakers, surge protection, earthing and installation, and for a grid-tied system the net-billing application. Mosque committees often collect donations against a quote: ask for an itemised quote so donors can see what each part costs.

mistakes: Sizing a mosque from its yearly bill. The winter bill is small and the summer Zuhr load with ACs is large; the panels must carry the summer running load at midday.
Using the default list without checking. The mosque and shop lists are estimates; count your own fans, lights and ACs and the hours they run.
Forgetting the water pump for wudu. It runs for a short time but its starting surge sets the inverter's surge rating.
Sizing a battery for every load. Night prayers usually need fans and lights only; list those alone for a battery you can afford.
Assuming a domestic tariff for a shop. Shops are billed on the commercial tariff; use the rate on your own bill for the saving.
safety: A solar system connects to the building's wiring and the grid at mains voltage, and a mosque or shop has many people under the same roof. Have a licensed electrician and a DISCO-approved installer do the wiring, earthing, protection and the net-billing connection, and keep the inverter and batteries in a ventilated room people do not use.

faq.q: How many kW of solar does a mosque need?
faq.a: The small one-hall mosque here needs about {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW with a {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter; the larger mosque with 2 ton ACs about {{ex.1.out.installed_kw|2}} kW. Enter your own fans, lights, ACs and hours for your figure.

faq.q: Can a mosque run its ACs on solar?
faq.a: In daylight, yes: Zuhr and Asr fall in full sun, and the panels are sized so the running load of {{out.running_w|int}} W, ACs included, runs on sun at midday. Maghrib, Isha and Fajr run from the grid or a battery.

faq.q: What size solar system does a small shop need?
faq.a: About {{ex.2.out.installed_kw|2}} kW with a {{ex.2.out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter for lights, fans, a deep freezer, a computer, CCTV and Wi-Fi through the day, and about {{ex.3.out.installed_kw|2}} kW with one inverter AC.

faq.q: Does a mosque need a battery with solar?
faq.a: Only for power during load shedding after dark. A grid-tied system without a battery is the cheapest and covers the daytime prayers; add backup hours above for Maghrib and Isha, listing fans and lights only.

faq.q: How much does a solar system for a mosque cost?
faq.a: Prices change with the dollar rate, so we do not print one here. Use the solar price estimator for the current range for {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW, and ask installers for an itemised quote.

faq.q: Where do the mosque and shop load lists come from?
faq.a: They are Wattlyst estimates from typical small mosque and shop fit-outs in Pakistan, with appliance watts from our appliance list and summer hours. They are starting points, not measurements; every row can be changed.
